summary: EmberMed: control-plane heartbeat spike causing session GC flaps, streaming stalls, and failback churn
description: Summary: During a sustained outbound heartbeat burst from the control-plane to tenant brokers, EmberMed saw cascading session GC (garbage-collection) on their private tenancy which triggered repeated failbacks to the hosted pool. Symptoms included streaming stalls where clients saw silence (no tokens) for 3–12s, intermittent 5xx responses, and an elevated token billing delta. The customer experienced degraded SLAs and opened an escalation call.
impact: Approximately 85% of EmberMed's active API sessions experienced at least one streaming stall during the incident window. Latency tail (p99) for streaming increased from ~120ms to 5.4s. Some requests retried which led to a billing delta estimated at ~1.8x normal token spend for the affected window.
steps_to_reproduce: 1) Customer connected long-lived streaming sessions to their private tenant in us-east-1. 2) Simulate high-rate control-plane heartbeat (interval reduced to 200ms) across ~1200 session workers. 3) Observe broker CPU/memory thread contention, leading to session GC events and upstream failback policy activating. 4) Resulting streams stall or close and clients retry.

investigation_notes: Hypothesis: The control-plane rollout inadvertently set heartbeat jitter to zero for performance tuning, which caused many tenants to simultaneously issue heartbeats. The broker admission and session GC logic was not resilient to synchronized spikes, leading to thread stalls and failback triggers. Reproduced locally by forcing synchronized heartbeat timers across worker pool. Verified that adding jitter and increasing intake queue reduced contention.
mitigation_steps: 1) Immediately re-enabled heartbeat jitter and increased default heartbeat interval for high-concurrency tenants. 2) Throttled control-plane rollout for tenant-targeted flags. 3) Performed rolling restart of EmberMed broker to clear GC backlog. 4) Issued a temporary billing credit hold while investigation continued.
resolution: Applied a hotfix to the control-plane to reintroduce randomized heartbeat jitter and increased broker intake queue sizes; rolled patch to affected brokers in us-east-1. Confirmed with EmberMed on-call that streaming latency returned to baseline and no further failbacks occurred. Finance issued a one-time credit for the incident window; customer accepted the remediation.

post_incident_notes: Root cause: regression from a control-plane optimization that removed heartbeat jitter. Contributing factors: lack of per-tenant intake backpressure controls and insufficient synthetic tests for synchronized-control-plane signals. Positive: hotfix effective and customer regained service quickly. Long-term: pursue per-tenant isolation and more exhaustive rollout tests.
resolution_summary: Hotfix + broker restart stabilized streams; customer credited for excess billing; runbook and monitoring improvements scheduled. Incident closed after verification window of 48 hours.
